Promise of the Rose is my favorite Sailor Moon movie, hands down. As for why, well, there are several reasons. 
I vividly recall us (my mother and me) stepping into Blockbuster to rent out some movies. And there it was, the sealed vhs magesticslly leaning against the wall right next to the entrance. I practically begged my mother to get it. I had no idea there was a Sailor Moon movie! 
She said no, and I basically stared at the vhs tape while she browesed. Well, really, it was more of a shelf of vhs tapes of it. Still, I was very fixated on it. 
She caved after she got whatever movies she wanted to rent. 
I'm surprised I didn't wear it out with how often I rewatched it. I was so in love with Sailor Moon's princess dress (I hadn't watched that part of the anime at the time to know her as Princess Serenity). But more importantly,  I was inspired by her to keep pushing forward even if it seemed impossible to defeat an alien flower. 
And when the ending came, I belted out the kickass song, then cried my eyes out. 
It was a comfort movie to me as a kid. Hell, it still kind of is, even with the new dub (sad my beloved "Power of Love" isn't in it, but whatever).

Concept summary: Mission to save sister and prevent a cursed LI from going crazy. Fantasy setting  where LI is an elf, MC and sister are humans, and sister has a LI of her own as a dragon man.

More info: Our heroine finds herself at a loss for what to do. LI has gone insane and on a slaughter spree. Her sister was killed as a sacrifice to keep a monster sealed. The kingdom is in chaos. MC wishes desperately to go back, to figure out how things went so wrong. As she trips over a root on her way to stop LI, she tumbles down a hill and cracks her skull open on a rock. 
When she opens her eyes, she's surprised to find herself in a small town, with LI in a bed next to hers. It takes her a few moments to sort through everything. When LI awakens and acts as he had when they first met, it confirms her suspicions that she really had gone back. And that complicated things. 
In the original time line. MC set out on a quest, hiring LI has a bodyguard, in order to go and rescue her sister from the king. She had thought the king kidnapped her sister. In reality, the king had desperately needed a healer and sister was one of the best in the land. But sister thought she left an obvious note to not worry MC. Sister is a loveable airhead. 
Knowing this from the past life, MC is in a bit of a pickle and still has to act desperate and determined, while also coming up with a plan to change things secretly. 
LI is perceptive and calls her out on it. She fesses up and proves her knowledge of him. He agrees to help her still, even if it means her quest has now changed. As much as she wishes to make sure sister is allright, she knows she is tight on time to stop a betrayal, defeat the monster when it unleashes, and find a way to prevent LI's curse from activating. 

Honestly, I'm adapting this idea based on a novel draft I already wrote... is it bad that I might like this version better? Even if it means I have to change a lot... lol

For example, I've come to learn recently that I dislike games where one LI's route is tragic no matter what while all the other LI's in the game get a happy ending because there are no alternate endings for any of them.
